```renyi
public function statement_line(order: Invoice) returns Text
  purpose: One row of the statement: customer, number of lines and total, in fixed columns.
  example: statement_line(Invoice(customer: "ACME", lines: [], discount_percent: 0))
    is "ACME          0 lines      0.00"

  let name_column be order.customer.pad_right(10)
  let count_column be order.lines.length().to_text().pad_left(5)
  let total_column be invoice.total(order).to_text().pad_left(10)
  return "{name_column}{count_column} lines{total_column}"
end
```

```
public function statement_line(order: Invoice) returns Text
  purpose: One row of the statement: customer, number of lines and total, in fixed columns.
  example: statement_line(Invoice(customer: "ACME", lines: [], discount_percent: 0))
    is "ACME          0 lines      0.00"

  let name be order.customer.pad_right(10)
  let count be order.lines.length().to_text().pad_left(4)
  let amount be invoice.total(order).to_text().pad_left(9)
  return "{name} {count} lines {amount}"
end
```

The example gives only one row, so I inferred the column widths from it: customer padded to 10, line count to 4, total to 9, with single spaces between the columns. I did not check the exact count of spaces beyond that one example. I also assumed `pad_left` and `pad_right` take a width and pad with spaces, and that a `Decimal` rounded to 2 places prints as `0.00`.
